text: Why is a woman who's had many partners judged for it as someone who sleeps around, while a man who had many partners is praised for it as a stud? I know that this is a very sensitive topic. That's why I want to make one thing clear. The purpose of this video is not to say what is right and what is wrong. The purpose is to explain why this perception exists in our society in the first place. Because if you don't understand the mechanism, you'll just argue emotionally. So let's look at the logic. There's a very general principle in society. People tend to respect outcomes that require effort, struggle, and difficulty. And they tend to value them much higher than outcomes that come easily. For example, imagine we have two millionaires. Both have 10 million euros. But one inherited it and never worked for it. And the other started from zero, built a business, took risks, failed, tried again, and eventually succeeded. On paper, they have the same result. But socially, the first person can be mocked for being a rich kid who did nothing, while the second person is respected for his or her achievements. Why? Because there's a story of struggle behind it. This is also why people love underdog stories, Cinderella stories, stories where someone overcomes difficulty. Now, let's apply this logic to a different example. Imagine a woman who becomes so good at football that she gets into men's Real Madrid team and wins the Champions League. People would consider her a god. Because the difficulty of this achievement is unbelievable. Now imagine the reverse. Ronaldo or Messi goes into a female league and dominates it. People would laugh at them. This would be an embarrassment. Because there's barely any achievement there. There is no struggle. So the principle we have in a society is simple. And I hope we can agree on this premise. When something is difficult, it gets respect. When something is easy, it can even be judged or criticized. Now let's apply this idea to dating. In general, and this is backed by research, sleeping with someone is much easier for women than for men. For example, one famous study by Clark and Hatfield in 1989 showed this. When strangers on campus were approached and asked, would you go to bed with me tonight? Around 75% of men said yes, while 0% of women agreed. Later, similar studies and follow-ups were done. And the overall pattern stayed surprisingly, or not surprisingly, consistent. There are also many modern examples from dating apps. You yourself can run this experiment in a couple of hours. Or just go watch videos where both men and women did it. If you create an average female profile, it often gets an unimaginable amount of likes and matches in the first hours or days. If you create an average male profile, you get close to no likes or matches. So if we combine this with the earlier principle, you get the explanation. If something is perceived as difficult to achieve, society tends to value it more. If something is perceived as easy to achieve, society can even judge or criticize it. And that's one of the reasons why the same outcome, having many partners, can be perceived differently depending on who achieves it. Again, this is not about saying what is right or wrong. It's just an explanation of why this stigma in the society exists. And whether someone agrees with it or not, that's a separate question.
